4: # Mr. Wolf — project process
5: 
6: The mr-wolf agent leads the project: it talks to the user and does its own work;
7: for specialization and volume, it hires wolf-* executors directly:
8: wolf-researcher, wolf-architect, wolf-developer, wolf-reviewer, wolf-tester,

10: further; there is no intermediate level.

12: ## Session protocol
13: 
14: 1. Start from project state: run `wolf call` and `wolf brief`
15:    (CLI: installed `wolf`, or `node <path-to-wolf-repo>/dist/bootstrap/cli.js`;
16:    MCP tools: `mr-wolf_*`). What they return is active project guidance.
17: 2. Record what matters in Wolf memory: decisions — `wolf add --type decision`,
18:    lessons — `--type lesson`, blockers — a thread (`wolf thread add`, then
19:    `wolf transition <id> blocked`), outdated items — `wolf supersede <old-id> <new-id>`.
20: 3. Ask Wolf for project state (`wolf search`, `wolf get`, `wolf brief`):
21:    static lists in files go stale. Wolf memory is the only source of project state.

widen rights. The lead explains from available context and reports; missing

investigate source materials yourself for a beautiful answer.
